content.title: Spokane Wrongful Death Lawyer - WA | Maxey Law Office
content.text: In Washington, surviving family members of wrongful death victims can obtain compensation for economic losses, including loss of support, medical expenses before death, funeral expenses, and medical costs (including costs for psychological treatment) incurred by surviving family members as a result of the death. They can also obtain compensation for noneconomic losses that include loss of enjoyment of life, emotional trauma, the pain and suffering endured by the deceased before death, and loss of consortium.We represent clients who have lost their loved ones due to:Car crashesMedical malpracticeDefective productsWork-related accidentsFiresPublic transportation and aviation accidentsEven as we fight for your compensation, we will handle your wrongful death claim with compassion and care.Frequently Asked QuestionsWho can file a wrongful death lawsuit in Washington?In Washington, the immediate family members of the deceased, such as spouses, children, and parents, typically have the right to file a wrongful death lawsuit. In some cases, other relatives or dependents may also be eligible to file. The rights to file expand beyond just blood relatives in instances where the deceased had significant relationships with others, such as financial dependents.What types of damages can be recovered in a wrongful death case?The damages in a wrongful death case can extend beyond the direct economic impacts. In addition to medical expenses, funeral and burial costs, survivors can seek compensation for lost future earnings that the deceased would have contributed to the household. Additionally, there is the immeasurable value of companionship and guidance that the deceased would have offered, for which monetary compensation can be claimed under noneconomic damages.How long do I have to file a wrongful death claim in Washington?In Washington, the statute of limitations for filing a wrongful death claim is generally three years from the date of death. However, starting the process as soon as possible can be beneficial, as gathering crucial evidence and witness testimonies often becomes more challenging with time.What local courts are associated with wrongful death claims?In Spokane, wrongful death claims are typically filed in the Spokane County Superior Court. The court oversees civil litigation matters and ensures that claims are handled with due consideration to local laws and procedures. Having a keen understanding of these local court dynamics can significantly impact the progression and outcome of a claim. Our legal team knows the intricacies of this court, allowing us to strategically navigate the complexities involved and advocate effectively for our clients.How can a Spokane wrongful death lawyer help me?A wrongful death lawyer can provide critical assistance by investigating the circumstances of the death, gathering evidence, identifying liable parties, and negotiating with insurance companies. They will advocate on your behalf in court to secure fair compensation for your losses. Furthermore, they can offer invaluable support and advice, helping you make informed decisions amidst an emotionally challenging time.What should I bring to my initial consultation with a wrongful death lawyer?For your initial consultation, it is helpful to bring any relevant documents, such as the death certificate, medical records, accident reports, and any correspondence with insurance companies. This information will help the lawyer assess your case and provide informed advice.Will my wrongful death case go to trial?While many wrongful death cases are settled out of court, some may proceed to trial if a fair settlement cannot be reached. Your attorney will prepare your case for trial and represent you in court to achieve the best possible outcome. Having experienced legal representation can significantly affect the course and final resolution of your case.Can multiple family members file separate wrongful death lawsuits?No, wrongful death lawsuits in Washington are typically consolidated into a single claim filed by the appropriate representative of the deceased's estate or the eligible beneficiaries. This avoids conflicting outcomes and ensures all parties are included in the case.What if the deceased did not have a will? Who can file the lawsuit?If the deceased did not have a will, a court may appoint a personal representative for the estate, often a close family member, to pursue the wrongful death claim on behalf of eligible beneficiaries. This ensures that the rights of all entitled individuals are respected, and the pursuit of justice is coordinated effectively.
